Date: November 7, 1972

RICHMOND, VIRGINIA

PHILIP MORRIS
U.S.A.
INTER-OFFICE CORRESPONDENCE

To: Mr. F. E. Resnik

From: P. A. Eichorn

Subject: . Parliament Cigaretts

I have reviewed all existing files on the Parliament cigarette including work done by Lee Harrow and have discussed the subject with Messrs. Osmalov, Claflin, Wickham, Daniel, Tindall, Meyer, etc. I have been able to identify only one possible technical aspect that might be used in connection with promotion of the recessed filter. The claim might be made that, "millimeter for millimeter the Parliament recessed filter is the most efficient filter in the world" (except for diluted CA filters). This claim is supported by the fact that the cellulose acetate used in the filter has a denier of 2.2 and contains approximately fifty thousand fibers in a 15 mm space compared to other conventional cellulose acetate filters which have a denier of 2.9-3.0 and contain approximately forty thousand ± fibers in a 20 mm space.

1001915496

Other ancillary comments include:

1. Recessed Filter: No tar and nicotine from the filter onto the tongue. Earlier studies show that a flush filter has potential of transferring 10-100 micrograms of tar (with nicotine) onto the tongue - but - no transfer from the recessed filter.

2. Recessed filter is distinctive and unique among filters. It is a visible, easily identified difference which sets Parliament apart from all other cigarettes. The combination of a different filter and special tobacco blend provides a unique product.

[SIGNATURE] P.A. Eichow

3. Parliament sales have held consistently at approximately 2% of the market for ten years. At this sales level, it has been one of the steadiest sales lines on the market. This consistent sales pattern makes it evident that there is a specific category of customer who is loyal to Parliaments for its smoke/flavor characteristics and image. The image is one of elegance and cleanliness. It is the "up-town" or "country club" type of product which reflects personality and quality.

cc: Mr. R. Graham
